name: Sumatra Mandheling G1, Aceh
vendor_notes: Chocolate, cedar, sweet tobacco and spice; mild acidity, creamy body. Spicy, earthy, fruity and flowery 4/4.
goal: Dark roast: chocolate, cedar and spice with heavy body, low acidity
rationale: Wet-hulled Sumatra is irregular in size and carries more moisture, so it needs a steady, energetic start (charge 190 C) to dry evenly. For a dark roast the development is long: ~23 C after first crack over ~3 min (DTR ~28%), finishing around 211 C on this probe, at or just before second crack. RoR is kept ~10 at FC and only eased to ~6 by drop, so the roast keeps moving: a stalled dark roast tastes baked and flat. Air goes up for the heavy smoke. Stay with the roaster near the end.
steps: Preheat to 190 C, then hold steady 10+ min (BT/ET flat).
Charge 170 g at BT 190. Burner 72%, air 30, drum 90.
TP ~0:42 near 103 C. RoR peaks around 1:30.
At 178 C (~6:32): burner 50%. RoR ~10 and falling.
FC ~7:30 at ~188 C: burner 46%, air 60. Then 44%.
Drop ~10:25 at ~211 C, or at first 2nd-crack snaps (press SCS).

history.note: Initial plan (for a family member) from the Coffee Bean Corral page and the 2026-09-29 calibration: TP ~0:40, Honduras FC 188.9 C, burner steps ~2 min before FC.
